text: There's good dirt under all this moss. Who's been using it?
I can't go on... come back for me.
Water near, for the beds and the flax.
You're not from the village. Doesn't matter. Help me with this sack.

I was found guarding seed at a burnt farm in the deep woods. There's another in the Hollow Pines, my grandmother said: burnt the night the hearth went out, and somebody kept a fire going there after the roof was gone. I want to know what for.
Iron chafes. It wants linen under it. Build me a tailor's shop by Gunnar's lodge and I'll weave it, four bolts to start.
You gather what the woods drop. I grow what they won't. Give me the Farmer's work and a plot of turned earth, and it grows while you're away.
Water by the beds. The barley drinks, and I don't carry it as far.
It came up. Their seed, in their field. I'll keep it for them.
A Farm Plot. Turn the earth somewhere it gets the sun.
Light the Hollow Pines' stone, and I'll sow their seed where they meant to.
South, in the Hollow Pines. A longhouse with no roof. Look at their hearth.
The Tailor's Shop at Tier II, four Linen, and the Weaver's work for me.
They meant to come back. Follow the burnt fence and see how far they got. Take planks: whatever they left will be falling down.
I'm from past the ridge. I walked home last spring and the road went somewhere else, and my village wasn't at the end of it.
And the rain came home to the furrow, and the furrow came home to me.
I planted a row of the old barley. From home. Only six seeds were left.
My mother sang this at the sowing. I've forgotten half the words.
The barley came up thick on the east bed.
The first sheaf goes back in the ground. The second is yours.
The short way is round. Round the beds.
We'll eat it together. My mother would have liked you.
Your boots were in my beds again. The flax won't stand now.
Behind you!
Watch your back!
I owe you one.
Still here. Still here.
Thank you. I thought that was it.
I can't take much more of this.
I'm hurt!
I'll hold this spot.
I'll keep back.
Nothing gets to you without going through me.
Point the way.
Right behind you.
Here they come!
Weapons up!
Clear. Get your breath.
That's the last of them.
I came to examine the old iron markers. Whatever protects the road has cracked. Steel will help tonight, but steel alone will not mend this.
We came to learn why this forest has become bewitched. First, we need shelter. Follow the old road.
Hold still. Drink this.
Not yet, you don't. Drink.
You're bleeding. Here.
Stay near the stones. We can still get out of this together.
Anything else?
Smoke's going straight up. Fair day, then.
Someone saw Ingrid out there, walking in circles. Walking. Do you understand? Go and look.
Where's the anvil? No, don't tell me. I'll find it.
Tell Sigrid I kept it lit.
A smith's bones like a warm house. The forge is warm enough by day.
You took your time. Mind the hammer.

Copper wants a hotter fire than this hearth gives. Raise the Smithy a tier. The fire's bigger then, and so's the bench: put a loft over it for what's done, and the queue won't stop when the work changes. Then make yourself a copper pick.

My grandfather cut stone before he ever worked iron. The boundary stones came out of a quarry in Ravenwood, he said, north of here, and the masons cut more than names into them. They left one half done. Take two ingots of copper for wedges, and finish it.
There's copper in these woods, and charcoal in any oak you leave smouldering by the fire. Bring me ore and coal, and we'll smelt three ingots.
There's iron in the barrows. Grave iron, the old ones called it: it holds an edge and it holds a chill. Three pieces, and I'll face an anvil with it. What comes off that anvil comes off better.
You found me. Then let me earn my bread. Give me the Smith's work and a Smithy, and nothing you carry out there stays broken for long.
Warm through, for once. My bones thank you before I do.
Ravenwood again. I'll go up of an evening and cut what they started. Iron can wait an hour.
A Smithy, and the Smith's work. Then bring me something worn and see what half the cost looks like.
Copper ore and charcoal. Three ingots at the Smithy. Leave oak in the campfire for the coal.
Light Ravenwood's stone. It stands by the path through the wood.
The Old Quarry, north. Two copper ingots for the wedges, and the stone they never finished.
The Smithy at Tier II, a Storage Loft from its Upgrade tab, then a Copper Pickaxe.
Three Grave Iron from the barrows, and the Smithy at Tier III for the anvil.

I blazed the trees going in, a cut every twenty paces. Coming back, my marks were on the wrong side of them. The road hadn't moved. The roots had moved it, under us, in the night. Tor was thrown further in than me, with a bad leg. Listen for a saw where nobody saws.
Iron is best worked at dawn. Always has been.
It is now. I'm the one with the hammer.
It is soft. That's why it needs good nails.
My iron cracks because it's cold. Not because of your scratching.
Strike once for the iron, strike twice for the blade!
Then cut slowly, old man.
Then sleep further from the forge.
You've been at my anvil with chalk again.
Behind you!
Watch your back!
I owe you one.
Still here. Still here.
Thank you. I thought that was it.
I can't take much more of this.
I'm hurt!
I'll hold this spot.
I'll keep back.
Nothing gets to you without going through me.
Point the way.
Right behind you.
Here they come!
Weapons up!
Clear. Get your breath.
That's the last of them.
I trust that she wants to get out of here alive. That is enough for tonight. But watch her hands when she talks about the stones. She knows more than she says.
My sister's farm is two valleys from here. Her dogs ran into these woods last month and never came back. Someone has to walk in front. Better me than you.
Once, as a boy, with my sister. Spruce, moss, the quiet you get in old woods. Nothing in it frightened me but the dark. I would like that to still be true.
Twenty winters in the shield wall at Granheim. I stopped counting the fights a long time ago. I still count the friends.
Wolves, probably. Perhaps a witch, perhaps a sick troll. It is usually less than the stories and more than you packed for. Four friends, if we are lucky. Byarna owes me money.
Eat something, even if you are not hungry. I have buried enough friends who thought they could fight on an empty stomach.
Stay between me and the trees. If anything comes out of the dark, it meets my shield first.
Hold still. Drink this.
Not yet, you don't. Drink.
You're bleeding. Here.
Eat something. It is a long road, and the porridge is not getting any better.
Go! I will hold them. Nobody gets left behind, not while I am standing.
Anything else?
Heard the deer down by the trees at first light.
Up early? The portal hums louder before the sun.
Come back when it's done.
Before we set out? Gladly. Take this practice sword; it bruises, it doesn't cut. Hit the dummy by the fire until your arm knows the way, then come and try it on me.
Now that is a fine idea. Anything but this porridge. Here is a rod and a handful of grubs, and the lake is just south of the road. Two fish, and I'll owe you.
We always need firewood. Take this hatchet; there are good trees on the slope north of the road. Six logs will do us.
Breakfast! You may be the best person on this expedition. Keep the rod; there is bound to be water in those woods.
That will keep us warm. Keep the hatchet.
You'll do. Better than most I have trained, worse than you will be. Take these; you will want them.
Dummy first, then me. Watch my shoulders: the blow is coming when they drop.
Six logs from the slope north of the road. Walk up to a tree and get chopping.
Two fish from the lake. Hold attack to swing back, let go to cast, and strike when the float goes under.
Show me the wall. Then show me where it's weakest.
Behind you, you fool!
Go. I've held worse.
Still got one more swing in me, then.
Ugh. Took your time.
Twenty winters, and it still hurts.
A lit way home. I've seen what waits in the dark.
Don't look at me like that. I was resting. ...Thank you.
My knees are too old to run from a closing portal. Next time leave earlier.
That many, and I'm still here. Don't tell the young ones. They'll want to try it.
Twenty winters I've been telling that kind of story. First time it's been true.
Took you long enough. How many are behind you?
Finally, something I can hit.
Stay behind my shield, if you can find it.
A watch that leaves its post has a reason. The old tower stands on the edge of the Wolfwood, south-west past the fen. Find out what theirs was.
I kept watch for the expedition until there was nothing left to watch. Let me do it here. A post with a view of the old path, and the ward holds longer when it breaks.
My sister Sigrun sewed a red thread into my coat before I left. Said I was too stupid to find my way home without it. That valley's full of old camps. If one of them has her thread in it, I want it.
The Brukam's dead and its tusk is lying out there. Hollow it, bind it in iron, hang it on the post. When the ward breaks I'll blow it, and every one of us will shoot like we mean it.
When the ward breaks they come through the gaps. Spikes in the gaps, three at least, and we hold the next one together.
A lit way home. I walk it slower now, and that's a good thing.
The Old Grey. My grandfather would have stood a round for whoever did it. I'll keep the fire at the tower.
A camp half under the snow in Troll Valley. A red thread. Bring it to the portal.
A Watch Post where I can see the old path. It wants Tor's lodge standing first.
Light the Wolfwood's stone. Then I keep the watch out there.
The Brukam's tusk, and the Watch Post at Tier III to hang it on. Then we hold the next breach.
The den is north-east of the tower, back toward home. Bring the old one down. Come ready.
The Ruined Watchtower, south-west. Read what they left by the door.
Three spike traps where they'll come through. Then hold the next breach.
Three days I held that clearing. At night something in Granheim mail walked the edge and never came in. I knew the walk. I couldn't give it a name, and I know every man I stood beside.
Clean your blade. It's a bad habit to forget.
Is that all? I was only warming up.
Fewer empty places this winter.
It's a wall. It'll be leaned on worse than that.
Never alone. That's the whole point of a wall.
Next time I'll let it eat the flax.
Seven went in. You still count us every night.
Then I'll go back for anyone. Tell them that.
Then I'll stand at the end of it tonight.
There was something by the fence at night. I went the short way.
Walls don't stop what's coming. People at walls do.
You were busy holding the rest of us together.
A soldier's choice. It is old iron, but it holds an edge. Guard well and let them come to you.
Eirik. Twenty winters in the shield wall at Granheim. I walk in front, I carry the heavy things and I make sure everyone eats. There is porridge. It is bad.
Long reach, and it wants both hands. If you ever need a light instead, press L to swap them.
She's alive.
Sigrun.
Somewhere is enough for now. Thank you.
The axe. Good. It splits wolves and firewood alike, and it leaves you a hand free.
Then we are after the same thing. We will find them.
A bewitched forest. My grandmother called any forest that ate her goats bewitched.
A whole day gone in a morning's walk. I don't like this, and I have liked very few things.
And the kindling you cut this morning is dry in your pack. We only need stones.
And there is only dry bread, unless someone fancies a walk. Ask me if you do.
Down you go. Catch your breath; we go again when you're ready.
Enough, enough! I yield. You'll do.
Good. Now me. When I wind up, raise your guard just before the blow, or roll through it.
Is it past noon already? We have not been walking an hour.
It is this place. At the tree line I had to think for my own sister's name. I did not like to say.
Nothing gets worse than this porridge.
Sigrid. The sun is going down. It was morning.
Steady now. It is a fine morning to walk into something stupid.
That trout this morning. I keep thinking about that trout.
Twenty years a soldier, and I have never seen the sun simply leave.
Whoever you came for: we have not stopped looking. Remember that.
Fire's lit. Come and sit, if you've a moment.
Too many fires in this place. A man can't hear the woods.
You've been frightening my deer. Least you can do is give me a roof.
I can't go on... come back for me.
Not far to the lodge. Meat won't cure itself.
Took you long enough. That boar's been lying on me since yesterday.
A raw hide rots. Cure four at the lodge and you'll see why the old hunters lived longer than the brave ones.
Boars come to the edge of the light at dusk. Bring me their hides and give me a lodge to cure them in, and you'll have leather that turns a tooth.

My grandmother said you hold a nykk with its own hair and steel in the water. Its hair makes a line the deep fish can't leave alone. The reeds in the Moss Marsh: it combs itself there. Two hairs. Don't say its name.
There's still water by the Haven. Fish it, if you like. Build a dock first, and don't say the name of the thing in the deep. It listens.
The lodge is close. The meat will thank you, and so do I.
A Dock on the still water, and one fish from it.
Cure four leathers at the Hunter's Lodge.
Four rough hides from the boars outside the light, and a Hunter's Lodge.
Two of its pale hairs from the Moss Marsh reeds, and the Dock at Tier II.
Twenty years I never lost a path in these woods. This year the paths started moving. Then the deer stopped running from me and started running from something else.
Boar again?
Fair. I'll see what the woods will give me.
I always go alone. That's why I come back.
I had a roof over my head for twenty years. The trees.
Nobody taught me. Everything that didn't learn it is dead.
One more set is a crowd. Fine. Tonight.
Something walked past the lodge last night. Big, and quiet.
You felled the old pine by the east path. The deer used it.
You never saw it. You were asleep.
Your rule. The woods have their own.
If you find any good cloth out there, I'll not say no.
Whoever laid this hearth had never met a level. I'll stay.
I can't go on... come back for me.
Close to the stone. Every walk is a block not cut.
Mind the coping. It's the only level thing for a mile.
Palisades burn. Granite doesn't. Raise the workshop again, cut four blocks, and put up four lengths of stone wall.
Wood burns. Stone remembers. Give me the Mason's work and a better workshop, and I'll show you a cottage with a proper hearth.
The stone's close. That's a block a day I'd have spent walking.
Byarna's Smithy standing, the Workshop at Tier II, then a Cottage.
The Workshop at Tier III, four Granite Blocks, and four lengths of Stone Wall.
Your hearth isn't level, your footings are soft and your walls are wood. Who cut these blocks? Not bad. I'll cut them from now on.
By trolls. Not by the Haven's own warden.
I've been watching how you set a beam. You were right about the snow.
My wall is the only straight thing in this valley. Your roof leans.
Once. That was the once.
Sing the half you have. The ground won't mind.
Then the snow and I agree on something.
There. Now the ground knows your voice.
You leaned your shield on my new wall. It's not dry.
Behind you!
Watch your back!
I owe you one.
Still here. Still here.
Thank you. I thought that was it.
I can't take much more of this.
I'm hurt!
I'll hold this spot.
I'll keep back.
Nothing gets to you without going through me.
Point the way.
Right behind you.
Here they come!
Weapons up!
Clear. Get your breath.
That's the last of them.
The plants are wrong. Roots that should sleep in this season are warm to the touch. Something is feeding the enchantment. Stay close; I brought a little medicine.
We came to learn why this forest has become bewitched. First, we need shelter. Follow the old road.
Hold still. Drink this.
Not yet, you don't. Drink.
You're bleeding. Here.
Stay near the stones. We can still get out of this together.
Anything else?
An altar to cleanse the curse? I know the old way. Build it, and I'll keep it burning.
Bog venom, carried carefully. It makes the strongest draughts. 4 Bog Venom, if you come across it.

I watched your fire for three nights from under a root. You should know two things. The old troll at the stones didn't come for us: it came for the door. And on the second night something walked past my root in Granheim mail, like Eirik's. I called to it. It turned, and it didn't know its name. When the stones broke I heard Byarna's hammer start up, somewhere deep in the woods, slow, like he's working one-handed. Let me be of use until we find them. Has no job yet.
My grandmother left bread on the old stones. Never hurts.

The expedition's alchemist, and the first of the seven to come home. She knows more about the curse than she lets on. Works as the Alchemist. Tends the Purification Altar, turning Cursed Essence into Purified Essence. Teaches you to build the altar.
Up early? The portal hums louder before the sun.
I kept saying the word so the forest couldn't take it. Fire. Fire. Fire. And then I saw yours.
I can't... go on. I'll hide here. Come back for me.
Clean water close by, for the work and for washing it off.
That's all of it. My grandmother would be appalled, and proud. Keep bringing me the curse; I'll keep it clean.
It's you! I saw a light through the trees and thought the forest had finally taken my wits. Get me out of here.
Clean. Feel how quiet it is? That is what the old ways spend. Bring me your blade, or whatever keeps you alive out there, and we'll give it some to drink. I've put a little by for the first.
It remembers now. One more thing, and then you know what I know: a mark, cut deep, that the forest can't easily undo. You know a few of the safe ones already, if you look.
It stands. It's crooked, and it's ours. Now the part that matters: bring me the Cursed Essence the woods leave on everything you kill, and we'll make it clean.
Somebody here knew what grows by alders, and what it is good for. There's a spring house in Alder Mere, west, gone dry. Clear it, and I'll have herbs the raids never bring me.
The altar cleans. Now something that heals. Build me a cauldron, and I'll brew you draughts that close a wound on the road. Make three and keep them close.
You came back for me. I won't forget it. Let me be useful: give me the Alchemist's work, and raise me an altar of rough stone where I can cleanse what the forest leaves on you. I'll show you where.
Water a few steps off. I can wash the work off before supper now.
Water in the basin again. Their herbs remember where they were planted.
Alder Mere, west of the meadows, above the water. The spring is choked with silt and stones.
At the altar, choose Empower. It shows you the price before you pay it.
At the altar, choose Enchant. One mark to a piece. The cursed ones can wait until you know what they cost.
Build the Cauldron, then brew three Healing Draughts at it.
Light Alder Mere's stone. I'll keep the beds.
Set it in the basin and leave it to me; it takes a while. Come back when there's some of it clean in the store.
Speak to me, give me the work, then six rough stone blocks and the life in four orbs. The Workshop squares the stone; the meadow stones hold the orbs.

I watched your fire for three nights from under a root. You should know two things. The old troll at the stones didn't come for us: it came for the door. And on the second night something walked past my root in Granheim mail, like Eirik's. I called to it. It turned, and it didn't know its name. When the stones broke I heard Byarna's hammer start up, somewhere deep in the woods, slow, like he's working one-handed. Let me be of use until we find them.
I borrowed it for an hour. The draught needed a wide pot.
It hums the way a kettle does before it sings. Or cracks.
Mine is cracked. Would you rather I let them bleed?
No. But it's honest.
Then we argue. Together, at the altar, tomorrow.
You read the stones better than I ever did. Tell me what they say about the curse.
Behind you!
Watch your back!
I owe you one.
Still here. Still here.
Thank you. I thought that was it.
I can't take much more of this.
I'm hurt!
I'll hold this spot.
I'll keep back.
Nothing gets to you without going through me.
Point the way.
Right behind you.
Here they come!
Weapons up!
Clear. Get your breath.
That's the last of them.
There are old paths here, older than the villages. My teacher said the waystones connected places of shelter. I thought that was only a story.
We came to learn why this forest has become bewitched. First, we need shelter. Follow the old road.
Hold still. Drink this.
Not yet, you don't. Drink.
You're bleeding. Here.
The stones are answering you. Stay close. I will try to keep the passage open.
Anything else?

Gear takes one mark at a time, cut at the altar with essence. Purified marks are safe. Cursed ones are stronger, and they always take a price: it's written on them, so you know before you cut. Nobody can teach a mark from nothing. It has to be found. The elites out there carry the mark that made them what they are: kill one and its inscription may be on it. The great ones, the trolls and the thing under the roots, carry great marks, the kind that change how a fight goes. And the carved stones in the deep woods: press a Blank Parchment to one and rub charcoal over it. Fiber and charcoal, nothing more. Bring the inscription home and read it here. Out there you'd only lose it in the mud. And mind this: a mark counts once, however many pieces carry it. Two of the same is one.
Mist's thick in the hollows today. Mind your step.
Your ward is a promise too. Did anyone tell you?
Write it down. Somebody has to write it down.
Somewhere to sit and read the stones.
The stones broke along a line. A line! Do you understand what that means?

Every rune you bring home is about the pact, and not one says what it was. The standing stones in Eastwood would. Whoever first made it, the Haven swore to it there. They read only by starlight, and cold stone wants warming: take a Hearth Ember.
Ingrid showed you the safe marks. I'll show you where new ones come from. Ask me how, then cut your first at the altar.
Runes aren't magic. They're promises the woods remember. Give me the work, and at Ingrid's cauldron I'll show you how to cut one for the road.
Somewhere to sit. The stones read better when my feet are still.
Keep the fire, and the wood keeps faith. I'll cut a rune at the stones now and then. They'll know what it's for.
Ask me about enchanting, then carve a mark at the Purification Altar.
Cut a Wayfinder Rune at the Cauldron. Ingrid will lend it.
Light Eastwood's stone. I want to read them myself, of an evening.
North-east, in Eastwood. After dark, with a Hearth Ember.
The stones broke along a line, straight as a chalk mark. Stones don't break straight. Somebody drew that line, and I want to know who.
Bring the old book. And don't hide the last page this time.
That isn't comforting.
That it remembers. Like us. That it can be argued with.
The marks on it were wrong. Your iron cracks because of them.
The ward hums louder after dark. Have you noticed?
Then explain the three blades that broke on the same mark.
Behind you! Turn!
On your back!
I owe you one.
Still here. Still here.
Thank you. I thought that was it.
I'm bleeding!
They're too close, I need room!
I'll hold this spot.
I'll keep back.
Nothing gets to you without going through me.
Point the way.
Right behind you.
Contact! I've got the range.
Moving, there!
All clear.
Nothing else moving.
Deer, boar, wolf, all running west out of the trees, out here where they don't belong. Nothing sleeps in the open unless it is afraid to sleep at home.
Poaching on the jarl's land. You learn to hit with the first arrow when the second one brings the wardens.
Someone is paying. And I would rather know what is coming out of there than wait for it to find me.
Troll tracks. Small ones, the moss kind. They never come this far down. Something is pushing everything out of the high woods, and it is big.
Walk where the moss is thick; it's quieter. Keep your back to the fire, never your face. And if you hear something heavy breathing, don't run until I say so.
I counted three wolves circling and one shape that was not a wolf. Keep your voice down. I would rather see them before they see us.
Tracks everywhere, all running the same way. Whatever they are fleeing, we are walking towards it. Lovely.
Hold still. Drink this.
Not yet, you don't. Drink.
You're bleeding. Here.
Nice morning. That is usually how it starts.
I will take the ones on the stones. You just keep breathing.
Anything else?
Wolves! They are not hunting; something is driving them towards us. Protect the camp!
More of them, coming round the other side!
Come back when it's done.

As it happens. There is a boar out on the grass north of the road, east of the camp, which is wrong all by itself, and we could use the meat. Take my spare bow: hold the left button to draw, let go to shoot. Bring it down.
Clean enough. Keep the bow; you've earned it, and I was tired of carrying it.
The boar, on the grass north of the road, east of the camp. Hold the left button to draw.
This place can be found. Good. So can everything else, by the same road.
Behind you! Turn around!
I know the way. Go on. I'll catch you up.
Bow's still good. So am I.
Move. I've got your back.
Too close, too close!
A light on the path. I come home late.
I counted our steps to the exit. I'd rather not count that close again.
I've tracked things my whole life, and never one that big. It left nothing behind but quiet. I don't trust the quiet.
The forest doesn't hate us. It doesn't notice us. That's worse. Next time I pick the way.
You crossed open ground to reach me. Stupid. Don't stop.
I've watched you for two days. You leave a trail like a cart.
I see them. Take the near ones.
There! In the trees!
I read ground the way you read faces. Give me the Tracker's work and every briefing names one more thing out there. Go through once and you'll hear it.
I walked those cairns once for a man in grey, counting stones. Now I want each to have one more from home, or the way forgets itself. The Lookout Cairn, then the Raven Cairn.
Something small takes from the camps and is gone before you turn. A tusse. Track one, and catch it before it slips away.
Light on my path. I came home late and saw every step of it.
The old ways are open. Touch any lit stone, and it knows the way to the others.
Go through the portal and come home. The briefing will have something more in it.
Light Westwood's stone, and the ways run between the lit stones again.
One tusse. They run the moment they see you.
West, on the knolls. A stone on each cairn.
I found my own marks on the wrong trees. Then I followed your light. A light doesn't move. That's the only reason I'm here.
Nothing else on the wind.
That's all of them. I think.
An elk. An old bull, lame in the left hind.
I come home at dawn. I sleep at dawn.
I saw where it stopped to rest. Twice.
Not alone.
The hammering starts before light. Every day.
Then walk with me tonight. Two sets of eyes.
There's a path past the north stones I don't like.
You walk like the woods taught you. Quiet on the outside of the foot.
A bow! Then there are two of us. Hold the left button to draw, let go to shoot. It wants both hands: if you ever need a light instead, press L to swap them.
An honest answer. I like you already.
It followed us! The old one, coming through the trees, right for the stones!
Liv.
Off the road, on your left! Rootlings. They were lying in wait, and they don't do that.
Runa. I find the tracks, and I shoot what makes them. Trolls off their crags, witches on the roads, wolves that don't run from fire. I want to see it for myself before I believe any of it.
Simple. I respect that. Hit it until it stops, and it leaves you a hand free.
A shepherd told me his dogs won't go past the tree line any more. Dogs. I have seen those dogs go after a bear.
Hold up. That's Byarna's handcart, tipped off the road. Have a look; I'll watch the trees.
Horses, running flat out, and not from us. Off the road!
It hasn't seen us yet. It will smell the smoke soon enough.
No birds. Have you noticed? Not one for a while now.
Sigrid. Look behind us. Where is the road? It was right there, and now there's only mist.
Still think the coin is worth it?
The shadows are wrong. They were behind us when we crossed the stream.
There. Feel that? The wind turned, and there is mist coming up off the moss.
Wolves behind them! In the open, in daylight. They don't do that. Weapons!
You shot straight this morning. It may matter before the night is out.
Your grandmother never saw wolves walk into a lit camp.
Behind you!
Watch your back!
I owe you one.
Still here. Still here.
Thank you. I thought that was it.
I can't take much more of this.
I'm hurt!
I'll hold this spot.
I'll keep back.
Nothing gets to you without going through me.
Point the way.
Right behind you.
Here they come!
Weapons up!
Clear. Get your breath.
That's the last of them.
Because the only old things out there are stones and roots, and the marks on them are older than any village. Whatever is wrong, I expect to find it written down.
Eirik sees a great deal for a man who pretends not to. Yes. I have seen stones like these before, and I know what they do. Ask me again when you have to touch one.
I know what it feels like: a door left open in winter. Someone opened it on purpose. Whether they meant to let something in or out... that is what we came to find.

Ingrid, Byarna, Tor and Liv. An alchemist, a smith, a carpenter and a scholar: the ones who can make sense of what they find. I sent them on two days ago to look over the old road. It was a short job.
Not in this dark. Ingrid's party went in on a night like this and did not come out. We sleep in turns, and at first light we... Quiet. Listen.
The cause. Trolls do not leave their crags for no reason, and wolves do not forget fire. Something in that forest has changed, and the villages want it named before it reaches their doors.
They did not send me. They asked for someone who could read the old marks, and I was the only one who answered. Draw your own conclusions. Everyone else does.
Words for things your tongue has no names for. Most of them mean wait. One of them means open. Pray we only need the first kind.
The villages think we came for wolves and witches. Let them. The stones out here are older than any village, and someone has been waking them.
Keep the torch high and the road under your feet. The forest is listening tonight. Let it hear only footsteps.
Hold still. Drink this.
Not yet, you don't. Drink.
You're bleeding. Here.
Take what time you need, but not too much. It is a long walk, and I want to be at the forest by noon.
Stand inside the ring. Whatever you see, do not let go of the stone until I say.
Anything else?
Count heads. Then count them again.
Heard the deer down by the trees at first light.
Not in this dark. Ingrid's party went in on a night like this and did not come out. We sleep in turns.
The road east is clear as far as the cart. Keep your eyes on the tree line, and stay close to the fire tonight.
The woods have names again. That is a start.
Then don't expect anyone to come looking.
Up early? The portal hums louder before the sun.
We set out at first light. Before that, is there anything you want to know about where we are going?
You're up. Good. The fire needs wood, and the stones need waking. Sit with me a while first.
Dry stone overhead. Good work. Now a fire, before anyone can think clearly: eight sticks and twelve small rocks off the forest floor, then build it beside the shelter.

The packs are tied and the fire is nearly out. Ingrid's party should have been back yesterday, and the forest is half a morning down the road. If you have anything left to do here, do it now: once we set out, we do not come back for it. Are you ready?
The rock shelter is along the old road, not far in. Go on, we are right behind you.
The stones are drawing power! Hold them off until the connection forms!
There you are. Come and stand by the fire with the rest of us. You should know who you are walking with before we set out.
Come back when it's done.
Hold together! Nobody gets left behind. We will find each other, whatever happens.
Finish your porridge and listen. This is the only quiet you will get today.
Stay on the road. We keep a steady pace, and the others will wait if you fall behind.
Seven went in. Tell me who's home.
Behind you! Move!
Don't you stop for me. That's an order.
Back in line. Thank you.
Good. On your feet. I mean, on mine.
Still standing. Barely.
Light on the lanes. People should see their way home.
A retreat is only a defeat if you learn nothing. What did we learn?
I gave you an order once to leave me if it came to that. You didn't. We'll talk about discipline. Later.
I've buried good people on less than what we just did. Write it down somewhere. It should outlast us.
I've served under worse than you. Don't let it go to your head.
You came back. I told them you would.
Form up on me!
Stand together! Nobody runs!
I led seven into those woods. I'll not lose the ones who came back. Give me the Leader's work and raise a banner where everyone can see it.

I led us north because I'd read of a road out of the Haven that the old ones took. It began at the Farewell Stones in Greyfell, I think, and whoever left by it cut their names there. Read them. Then cut ours under them.
Seven went in. Ask them what they remember of the woods, each of them. I need to know what I'm not being told.
Light on the lanes. People find their way home now. So do I.
Our names under theirs. Whoever comes after will know we went, and that we came back.
Ingrid, Byarna, Tor, Liv, Eirik and Runa. Ask each of them.
Light Greyfell's stone. The road starts at home again.
North-west, in Greyfell. Read their names, then cut ours under them.
The Haven Banner, where all of us can see it.
I heard your fire before I saw it. Every night a little louder. I knew it was one of mine. Nobody else in a hundred years would be fool enough to light one.
Count heads. Everyone still here?
Good. Move before more come.
Fewer. Not none.
I count the ones at the fire. Then I count the empty places.
I'm thanking you now.
We go out together and come back together. That's the rule here.
When the stones broke, you went back for Liv. I never thanked you.
You went past the north stones alone again.
...can anyone hear... Ingrid was right behind me when the stones broke. She's hurt. Find her first. Do you hear me? Find her first...
A fire. Sit down, all of you, and get your breath back. Whatever is out there will still be there when we are done.
Almost! Hold it off, just a little longer!
At first light we find the four who went ahead. Ingrid. Byarna. Tor. And...
Before we went in, I touched the middle stone. There were names cut into it, fresh, as if someone had only just carved them. Sigrun's was one of them.
Careful. The ones who go looking for the truth of it are the ones who find it.

For anyone who slept through last night's talk, and I know who you are: I am Sigrid, and we walk east today. The villages asked what is wrong in that forest. Two days ago I sent Ingrid, Byarna, Tor and Liv ahead to look. They should have been back yesterday.
I thought it was a list of the dead. I told no one, because I didn't want it to be true.
It will not wake for me. It never has. You, then. Put your hand on the centre stone.
I've kept something to myself since the day the stones broke. I'm done keeping it.
Liv. Of course. Eleven years I have known her, and for a moment there was a hole where her name should be.
Roots do not set ambushes on a road. Something taught them to. Keep moving. We need walls around us before more of them wake.
Then that's where we go.
We leave when you are ready. If you want to earn your porridge first, ask the others. They always have something.
Whatever you see, do not let go of the stone. There are things I should have told you, and there is no time left to tell them.
You asked me by the fire, so here it is. I have seen stones like these wake once. It took everyone who stood too near, and it put them somewhere else. Ingrid knew that when she came. Now you do.
I can see that. Light your torches, and take this one.
Keep walking.
Leave the fire! Take the old path north, to the standing stones. Now!
Not alone, and not before we are ready. Come back to the others.
Rumours grow in the telling. That is why we go and look, instead of sitting in a longhouse and listening.
Save it for the road. We have until the porridge gets worse.
That is no thunder. An old one, a mountain troll, and it is walking towards our fire.

That was no weather. The sun went down hours early and this storm came out of a clear sky. Ingrid, Byarna, Tor and Liv walked into this two days ago, so we go on, not back. Follow the old road into the trees and find us dry shelter. We are right behind you.
Wolves that hunt by day and do not fear four armed people. Whatever happened to this cart was quick, and it did not end here. We go on.
You wanted to know if the stories were true. How are you finding it?
And you. You came to us with a strong back and few questions. Nobody walks towards that forest by accident. Why are you here?
Then one thing first. Nobody walks that road unarmed. We carry spare arms in the packs. They are old and they are plain, but they will do. Take what suits you.
I opened a door like this once. I thought I could pull them through. The hunger came out instead.
I opened it a hand's width and heard her humming, and I closed it. If it had been her, she would have said Father. She only said that when she was frightened.
I ran. I left a village behind me with its names half eaten. I have been opening doors ever since, as if the next one would make it right.
There was a note on the table. Old Bear, find the blue door. She called me that when she wanted something.
Warmth stirs in the old stone. Little one. You fell out of the dark with the whole forest at your heels, and I caught you.
A fire first, little one. Fallen branches and loose stones lie all around me: pick them up, open the build menu and light it inside my ward. The sooner it burns, the sooner they can see it.
A held land asks something of you now and then, and its stone will tell you what. A Pact Rune laid in the stone holds it better still.
A horn at dusk, the expedition's signal. She is the last of them. Bring her home, little one.
A saw, out where nobody saws. Your carpenter is hurt, but he is still measuring.
A snare line, a mile of it, and at the end a man who did not mean to be caught.
A wall went up overnight out there, round nothing. Whoever built it will want to build a better one here.
Bare hands bring little home, little one. A hatchet in your belt and a pick beside it bring wood and ore. Sticks and sharp stones: make them in your bag.
Bring what my stones ask and lay it in me, then raise me. The deeper woods are waiting, and so are the ones lost in them.
Come and sit by me, little one. There is something I should have told you before you went to that hollow.
Find a place that a stone remembers, then lay your hand on the stone. The nearest stands not far past the meadows.
Go, little one. She is just beyond me, off the path. Come back through one of my doors before I close. What you wear I can always bring home. What you carry I cannot.
Listen, little one. Rest your hand on the stone.

Listen, little one. The guardian is old wood, and old wood fears one thing: fire. The trees out there weep a black sap when they fall. Boil it down around an ember from your hearth, and every blow you strike will burn.
Listen. A hammer, far off in the deep woods, slow and uneven. One of yours. Ask me what the woods hold before you go, and I will tell you where.
Marks on the trees that only the dark shows. Go through at night.
My ward keeps out the worst of the forest, not all of it. Put a wall between your fire and the trees.

North of the valley the old road goes on, little one, but I cannot see past its last bridge, at the valley's head. Something sits there that the trolls themselves pay. Go and look, and come home, and I will know the way.
Now bring me what you freed. Feed me that light and I will open for you, as I did in the dark.
Now feed yourself. Berries, water from the stream, a stew over your fire. You will be walking people home.

Now I know the way. It is a guardian, as old as my stones, and it will not wake for steel. Take an ember from your own fire to it. That, it cannot ignore. And come ready, little one: beyond my mist there is no turning back.
Now I know whose bridge it is. He was old when my stones were raised, and he has never let anyone cross for free. He waits on his own bridge over the gorge now. Go ready, or do not go.
Old stones are humming in the deep woods. Someone is inside the ring, writing.
One fire brought Ingrid home. The others will want more than a fire: a bench, a furnace, a dry place to set down what they carry. Build what they will need.
One weapon is one answer, and it will not last for ever. Make a second at your workshop: a club stuns what a blade only cuts.
She is close, little one. Just beyond me, off the path, hiding. Find her, keep her near you, and bring her through.
Smoke from a farmstead that burned long ago. Someone kept the seed.
Someone is cooking out there. The wolves can smell it. So can I.

Something breathes under the roots, little one. I feel it turn over in its sleep, deep in the Misty Woods, but I cannot see where. Find it for me. Walk into its hollow and come home, and I will know the way.
Something tests my ward. Out there, someone else is holding a clearing against the wolves. Bring him to hold mine.
The brighter this place burns, the further it can be seen. Build. Clear the old growth. Give them something worth walking towards.
The forest has put its roots in even here. Three stones around the clearing still hold my light, choked and cold. Free them, and bring the Life Orbs back.
The forest is gathering against your stone, little one. Stand watch beside it, or burn the rot's heart on a raid. It will not wait for you.
The light that reached her reached other things as well. They are on the old path now, testing me. Prepare yourself. When you are ready, tell me, and I will let them come.
What you carry through me, the woods can take from you. What you leave here, I keep. Build a chest beside your workshop, and put in it what you cannot bear to lose.
You brought the woods home on your back. Now make something of them: a lodge by the trees, a saw that turns logs into planks. The smithy and the walls start with a plank.
You have a fire. Now a roof to work under: a workshop beside it. What the woods break, it mends.
There is one memory the forest kept back from me, little one: who let my hearth go cold. The high tarn has it, and shows it only at night.

You came back to me torn, little one. I caught you, as I catch all of mine. But you met the dark with your mouth shut. The hird that built your hearths never did. Stand here and roar with me: let them be the ones who are afraid.
A hundred winters I kept this clearing alone. I had forgotten how loud a home is. Do not stop.
Every hearth in my light is a little more of the old pact kept.
I listen for your people every night. Some nights I hear them.
The forest cannot forget a place that someone tends.
A fire first. Then a home worth coming back to. Then we go and fetch them. And one day, little one, you will tell me why these old stones woke for your hand.
A lit stone said: this much of the forest remembers a hearth. Inside that ring nobody lost the way home, and nobody lost their name.
Did you see what grew out of them as they fell? Root. The same root that choked my stones, and closed the road behind your people.
Do you feel that? The ward has remembered what it is for. And far out in the mist, little one, someone has stopped walking and turned to look.
Every land you hold is a road home for whoever is still out there, and a door shut on what comes at night. Begin with the nearest stone.
Every name on that stone is someone the hunger has taken, or means to. The toll at the Brukam's bridge was never paid, little one. That debt comes due at the First Hearth.
Feel my stones: loose, where the roots held them for so long. I am a door that opens only a little way, into the near woods, where the mist is thin and young.

Find one of the places a stone remembers, so that it knows you, then lay your hand on it. The first will answer to my fire alone. The rest want a Pact Rune, the pact's own mark, scattered through the woods since it broke.
Further in, the mist is older. What lives there is stronger and hungrier, and so is what it keeps: better ore, older wood, and people who have waited longer than the ones you have found.
Good. Not all of them, and not all at once: only what you can hold.
He chose the closed door. That choice may be all he has left of them.
He is at his door again, under the road. Listen. I will carry his voice.
He is looking for two people the winter took. He opens doors to find them, and the wrong ones let things out.
He will feel it, wherever he is kneeling. I do not know yet if he will thank you.

I am a door, little one, and I have gone to sleep. I am too thin to wake myself. Long ago people kept a hearth beside these stones, and I kept the night from their door. That was the pact. No fire has burned here in a hundred winters.

I have not told you everything. The Heartroot was no monster. It was the forest's guardian: its half of the pact. Your kind let the hearth beside me go cold a hundred winters ago. It kept its half for ninety winters after that, alone, until the hunger got into its roots.
It called him by his name. That is how you know it lies: the ones he is looking for never used it.
It is all one thing, little one. Something old is pushing those roots, from somewhere deep in the woods. When the woods tell me where, I will tell you.
It is shut. That is the first thing anyone has undone for him.
It was not a list. The names were not a sentence. They were a warning.
It will. The pact gave the forest its room as well, and that is the one thing it has not forgotten. It will push against every stone you light. Hold what you take, and in time it leaves it be.
Its last word was for you. Hearth-keeper. Nobody has called anyone that in a hundred winters, and I did not teach it to you. One day you will tell me why these stones woke for your hand.
Keep the horse. Something has to remember them, and he cannot carry it any more.
Keep your own names close. Whatever is behind those doors has learned to speak in borrowed voices.
Lay the thread on my stone. Closer. Now, all of you, a hand near the fire.
Listen. Far off, at dusk, a horn: three long notes and a rest, over and over. The expedition's signal. Someone out there has seen your light and is answering it.
Little one. You have gone through me and come home, again and again. Each time you go, I hold the way open behind you. Each time, it costs me.
Look, now that there is light to see by. Three of my stones, choked in roots. And the roots are moving, little one. Slowly. Towards me.
My stones have gone quiet, but she is right. One spark burns close, just beyond me, hiding from the wolves. Make yourself tools, and go.
Once I am raised, the choice is yours each time you set out: the near woods, or the deeper ones. Go deeper when you are ready for what lives there, not before.
Seven sparks, scattered through the Misty Woods. They are alive. I hear them when the wind is right. But the forest does not kill the lost, little one. It forgets them.
She looked up. She heard something. Take the thread away, little one, before what is behind me hears it too.
So light one. The forest cannot forget a hearth that someone tends. It will feed my ward, and out in the mist your people will see it and know which way is home.
Somewhere.
Steady my stones. Bring what they ask and lay it in me, here, and raise me. Each time I am raised, a deeper tier of the woods opens, and I hold the way home open longer while you are out there.
Strength, which you will give me. And this: what is strong draws the hungry. The deeper I open, the more the forest will feel this fire. Keep your walls in good repair.
The last of an old promise. I keep the dark from this clearing. But that is not what you need to know.
Then she is still herself, and she is holding on. She will want the others home before her. Bring them, little one, and keep this fire high.
There. A hearth beside my stones, after a hundred winters.
There. A window, no wider than a book. A low room, a scarred table, a young woman with a needle between her lips, and a boy kicking at her knee.

When the hearth went cold, the stones went cold, one by one. The forest took back what they held, and every road and every name in it. That is where your people are now: out in the land that forgot us.
When the pact was kept, your people did not only tend a hearth beside me. They walked the land the pact gave them, and where it ended they set stones, and lit them from this fire.

With its roots gone quiet I can reach further. North, past the troll country, the road is open. The old one that broke my stones the night you fell walks that road. It came for the door then. Go carefully.
With what? You have nothing but your hands, and I cannot open.
Would you have woken it, knowing? It could not be saved, only stopped. Better by the hand of someone who keeps a hearth.
You brought it down. Lay what you carried out of the hollow by the fire, little one, where it can feel the warmth. It is owed that much.
You came for coin. There is none here. Stay anyway. They need you to.
You came for coin. There is none in this. But there is a debt now, and you have begun to pay it.
You came for someone. Every one of your people is out there because of what was let go cold. Bring them home, and the debt grows smaller.
You came looking for someone. Now there are others looking for you. Let them find a light.
You came to see if the stories were true. Here is the one nobody tells: we broke the pact first.
You came to see whether the stories were true. Now you are one of them.
You stood at his door. I felt it through the snow: a door that is not mine, and a man who has worn a hole in the world with knocking.
Your fire reaches further than it did, little one. Far enough that I can feel what lies at the end of it: stones, cold ones, out past the meadows.
Your people did, long before you were born. You are mending it. Every fire kept here is a payment on that debt.
And the guardian under the roots, who kept the forest's half. Where is it now?
And this. Their door, and the night kept from it, for as long as the fire burned.
Come and stand before me. You will see what the stones need.
Each holds a little of what I was. Free their orbs when you pass them, and I will hold the door a little longer.
He has been looking for it a long time. Go before he finds it alone.
Hold a ring of them round me, little one, and the forest will remember us for good.
I felt that. Out past the meadows, a stone remembers me again.
I know where the first of his wrong doors opened: the Black Pool, in the marsh. The fen came through it and drowned everything it touched.
I remember this. A fire beside my stones, and someone to keep it.
It broke against you. It will try again, somewhere else. Let it find you ready.
Keep it high, little one. A light is only a promise while someone keeps it.
Little one, behind you! My ward is too thin yet. They are coming up through it.
Little one, do you feel it? The forest is gathering against one of your stones. It means to push in.
Little one. My stones are loose where the roots were. Steady them, and I can open a wider way: deeper woods, and better things in them.
Little one. You have seen the road north now, and what walks it. Your fire reaches further than it did. Come and sit by me when you can: there is something out past my meadows you should know of.
Now it must be held, little one. A lit stone is a promise, and the forest will test it.
Past the Brukam's bridge the snow begins, and in it there is a door that is not mine. Someone is knocking on it, little one. Go and see who.
Rootlings, in my clearing. Feed me those orbs, and they will not get in so easily again.
Secure. Feel how still it is out there now. A land held that firmly sends home what it grows at every dawn, and the night's bands will not come through it.
Take an ember from the hearth, and shut it.
Three stones, and their light is mine again. There are more out in the meadows, little one: old ones the roots have not found yet.
With the marsh door shut I can see something under the valley's old road: a warmth, like a room someone still keeps.
Your fire carries now. Far past my meadows, those who went in with you will see it, if any are left to see.
First the way home. Then their names. Then there is no one left to find.
I can open the deeper way. But not as I am.
That is what you killed. I am sorry. Someone had to.
The stones are still out there. They only want a hand that keeps a fire.
Little one. You fell out of the dark with the whole forest at your heels, and I caught you. I could only catch one.
Behind you!
Watch your back!
I owe you one.
Still here. Still here.
Thank you. I thought that was it.
I can't take much more of this.
I'm hurt!
I'll hold this spot.
I'll keep back.
Nothing gets to you without going through me.
Point the way.
Right behind you.
Here they come!
Weapons up!
Clear. Get your breath.
That's the last of them.
This stone is dry enough. Give me sound timber and a little daylight, and I could make somewhere worth staying. For now, this fire will do.
We came to learn why this forest has become bewitched. First, we need shelter. Follow the old road.
Hold still. Drink this.
Not yet, you don't. Drink.
You're bleeding. Here.
Stay near the stones. We can still get out of this together.
Anything else?
A good joint takes the time it takes.
Best hour of the day, this. Nobody talking.
Fire's lit. Come and sit, if you've a moment.
I keep looking for Tor at the fire.
Up early? The portal hums louder before the sun.
It's built crooked, you know. All of it. Give me a week.
My tools. Leave them, if you have to. Not me.
A bench by the door, for the evening and my leg.
Still measuring. I knew someone would come, and I wanted something to show for it.
Logs are just weight until somebody cuts them true. Give me the Carpenter's work and a lodge by the trees, and I'll keep you in planks while you're out there.
More will come through that door, and they'll need a roof and somewhere to set down what they carry. A storage shed and a hut.
Ore weighs more than any pack. Raise my lodge a tier and I'll draw you a yard for carts. Barrows first.

The trees round the fire won't grow back as fast as we cut them. There are old cuttings past where the portal takes you. Send two of us out with food for the road, and we'll bring back what we can carry.
The ward keeps out the worst. Not all of it. Four lengths of palisade between the fire and the trees, and we sleep better.
There's a causeway sinking in the Drowning Fen, south, and good boards going to waste under it. Eight hardwood planks and it carries a cart again.
A bench by the door. I'll sit there tonight and admire your work. And mine.
Dry boards across the bog. Somebody will walk them who isn't running.
A Storage Shed and a Hut.
Four palisade pieces. Drag them out in a line; they go up like anything else.
Light the fen's stone. A road is only a road if it's remembered.
My lodge at Tier II, then the Wainwright's Yard, then a barrow from it.
South, in the fen. Eight hardwood planks.
The Haven's Lands. Pick who goes and where; they come home on their own.
The Woodcutter's Lodge, near the trees. Then cut me eight fine planks, so you see what it does.

There's a hollow in the deep woods where nothing grows, and the ground breathes there. In, out, slow as a sleeper. I lay three nights on this leg listening to it. Whatever is down there is old, and it's what moves the roots. Now, where do you want your planks?
And look how warm that kept you.
My roof leans on purpose. The snow slides off.
Say that again. Slowly. I want to remember it.
Strike three for the roof that keeps them dry! That's not how it goes.
The Haven used it. For a roof over your head.
Then I'll build you something stone can't do. A boat.
Thirty years I've cut wood. You're the first smith who didn't call it soft.
We both have hammers, Byarna.
You'll have my best oak for your hammer handles. Till I'm dead.
Your wall leans.
Mist's thick in the hollows today. Mind your step.
Show me your kitchen. No, on second thought, show me what you eat.
I can't go on... come back for me.
A warm hearth. A cook can't abide a cold house.
Mind the pot. If you've come to eat, you'll carry.
A cook is only as good as her fish, and the old fishers of Stillwater were the best the Haven had. Their rest is still on the shore, east. Bring me their nets, and three fish from that water.
Berries keep you walking. A meal keeps you fighting. Cook a broth at the Kitchen and eat it before you go through.
I cooked for a jarl once. He never thanked me either. A kitchen and the Cook's work, and you'll go out there fed properly.
A warm hearth. Come by later: the first loaf from it is yours.
Smoke in the reeds again. I'll keep the racks full.
A Forager's Broth from the Kitchen. Eat it before the portal.
Light Stillwater's stone, and the rest is ours.
The Fisher's Rest, east, on the shore. Their nets, and three fish.
The Kitchen. Byarna's Smithy has to stand first, for the pots.
They lit a lantern for their dead at the Netmender's Rest, south of the other, so the dead could find the isle. Go after dark.
Your fire's too small to cook on and too big to hide. Good. A fire is how lost people find a table.
A farmer who counts. I like you less already.
Bring me something that isn't boar and I'll cook something that isn't boar.
Everyone's mother liked me. It was the stew.
I cooked for a jarl once. He never once complained about the boar.
My pot is for food. Your swamp water goes in your own.
Something in my pot smelled of bog this morning.
Then I'll bake till my arms ache. Bring me the first sheaf.
Then the first loaf from it is yours, and nobody else's.
